This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed
investing to full-service wealth management all in one place. No matter your investing
goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Michigan Republican Senate candidate
Mike Rogers released an ad today calling for an end to President Trump's trade war with
Canada. Here in Michigan, we know that Canada is not our enemy. We need to end this tariff
war now. Rogers had previously defended some of the tariffs as necessary. It's the second
time Rogers has split with Trump recently after calling for an end to the Iran war, which
he previously supported. Asked about the ad today, Trump suggested Rogers wasn't breaking
with him on the issue, saying, "I viewed it as wanting Canada to make a deal." The Northern
Gulf Coast is bracing for the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, and Piers Debbie Elliott
reports the national hurricane season has posted a hurricane watch from the Louisiana-Mississippi
state line to Indian Pass in the Florida panhandle.
National Hurricane Center Director Mike Brennan says tropical storm ESA-ES is gaining steam
as it moves over the warm waters of the Gulf of Mexico.
ESA-ES is expected to be a strengthening, strong hurricane as it approaches the Northern
Gulf Coast on Friday into Friday night and Saturday. You can see multiple life-threatening
impacts from storm surge, heavy rainfall flooding, and hurricane force winds.
The governors of Alabama and Florida have declared states of emergencies, and the impending
storm has prompted school closures and event cancellations throughout the region. The Marine
Minerals Administration reports about 25 percent of offshore oil and 16 percent of natural
gas production in the Gulf has been curtailed. Debbie Elliott, NPR News.
The French government says it will pause the use of stun grenades in its policing of student
protests after a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off. The devices known as sting ball
grenades are meant to disperse protesters if the police are surrounded, as NPR's Elinor
Beardsley reports they're banned in most European countries.
"In a speech to the nation, Prime Minister Sebastien Le Corneux said contrary to what
people are saying, the police do not have orders to confront the students and are trying
to use proportional force in a difficult context. But there's been anger over what many say
are overly aggressive police tactics. Students and police faced off Wednesday in Paris for
several tense hours outside an elite university whose students have joined the high school
movement. The students chanted anti-police slogans from behind a barricade of trash bins
until the police charged with tear gas to eventually clear the street."
Elinor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
A top official at the World Health Organization says the U.N. health agency doesn't know how
a lab employee in Siberia died, but amid concerns about the plague, she's calling on Russia
to provide more information. Maria Van Kerkoff says the agency doesn't know what was the
causative agent behind the woman's death.
U.S. stocks pulled back from their record today. You're listening to NPR News from
Washington.
University of Arizona has suspended activities at its fraternities after reports of misconduct,
including assault and hazing. The school's dean of students says the reports involve nearly
half of the school's interfraternity council chapters. The suspension follows the recent
public outcry over how Cornell University handled fraternity rape allegations in 2024.
The federal housing agency HUD says it's investigating Wells Fargo for trying to boost
black homeownership. NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports.
In a letter to Wells Fargo's CEO, HUD says doling out loans based on race is no way to
do business, and it alleges the bank may have violated the Fair Housing Act. It's the latest
example of Trump officials going after equity programs that were created and encouraged
in the past to help rectify decades of federal policies that denied mortgages to minorities.
The black homeownership rate still lags far behind that of white Americans. In 2017, Wells
Fargo committed to helping close that gap with more loans. In 2022, it expanded a program
to refinance minority-owned homes. HUD's investigation was first reported by The Wall Street Journal.
Wells Fargo told NPR it had no comment. Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
A series of audiobooks the NHL launched to connect with fans of the hockey romance genre
is no longer available online. A league spokesperson says that the Hot for Hockey episodes were
specific to games during the opening week of the season. Hockey has picked up new fans
after TV shows Heated Rivalry and Off Campus featured the sport. This is NPR News from
Washington.

Tropical Storm ESA-ES strengthens in Gulf of Mexico, expected to become hurricane Friday
French government pauses use of stun grenades after 15-year-old's hand blown off during protests
World Health Organization seeks information from Russia about Siberia lab employee's death
University of Arizona suspends fraternity activities after reports of misconduct and hazing
HUD investigates Wells Fargo for allegedly violating Fair Housing Act with race-based lending programs
NHL removes Hot for Hockey audiobook series from online availability after opening week
